# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✋]

Right, I used an invalid symbol. My speech call was fine, I just need to drop the bad gesture call entirely.

```
speak(text="Display shows 6. Light is yellow. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute is pointing (👉) then giving 4 gesture marks (☝ ☝ ☝ ☝) — likely indicating "wire 4" or "position 4" in some counting scheme. Let me look at their earlier gestures: 👆☝, 👆✌, 👆🤟, 👆🖐, 👆✋ — this looks like they were enumerating wires 1-5 (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5) with 👆 as a prefix meaning "wire". Now 👉 followed by four ☝ symbols could mean something different — maybe "wire" pointer then repeating ☝ four times to mean "wire number 4" via tally, or it's a new symbol scheme entirely.

Since I can't be sure, I should just relay exactly what I received (blanks aside, I can see gestures) — but I can't speak gestures to Blind since gestures aren't heard, and Mute already knows what they sent. Actually my job is just to report the bomb visually; I don't act on Mute's gestures myself, I only see them. I have nothing new to add about the bomb (unchanged), so I'll just wait unless there's a change, but let me reconfirm the board is same and note I saw the gesture but can't interpret with certainty — no action needed from me except waiting since I can't speak to Blind meaningfully about wire selection since I didn't receive words.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new gestures arrived this turn, and the board is unchanged. I already reported the full bomb state to both Mute and Blind. Mute seemed to be asking about wire positions via gestures (likely confirming wire 4's color = green, based on their 👉☝☝☝☝ pattern matching their earlier 👆🖐 for position 4). Nothing further for me to add since I have no way to know what Blind or Mute need clarified without hearing speech.

I'll wait since I have nothing new to convey and don't want to spam duplicate information.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute is repeating the same gesture: 👉 followed by four ☝. This is likely a question they can't get answered because I haven't responded to confirm. Given their earlier enumeration (👆☝=wire1, 👆✌=wire2, 👆🤟=wire3, 👆🖐=wire4, 👆✋=wire5), this new prefix 👉 might mean "which one" or "confirm" applied to wire 4, or it could be a tally-count meaning "4" via four ☝ marks (i.e., "wire 4" spelled differently, redundant confirmation of wire 4 = green).

Since Mute repeated it, they likely are waiting for me to speak the color of wire 4 specifically. I already told them wire 4 is green in turn 1, but maybe they need me to confirm/re-state just that specific piece since Blind needs to act on it now. I'll speak clearly, isolating wire 4's identity for Blind (who receives my speech) and Mute (who also receives it, confirming they got the right one).

```
speak(text="Confirming: wire 4 is green.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute keeps repeating the exact same gesture every turn: 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝. This isn't a response to my confirmation — it seems to be a fixed message they queued, possibly sent once and I'm seeing it echoed each turn due to how visibility works, or they are stuck repeating because they haven't gotten confirmation from Blind and don't know I already answered (I can't be heard by Mute — wait, actually Mute CAN hear me, since I speak and "Mute and Blind receive it" per my channels).

So Mute should have heard my "wire 4 is green" twice now. Yet they keep sending the identical gesture. This suggests the gesture isn't asking about wire 4 at all — maybe it's unrelated to wires, and 👆/👉 distinguish two different things (like "display" vs "wire"), with the four ☝ representing the display number sequence, or possibly this is Mute relaying manual instructions via gesture (to me) since they can't speak... wait, Mute CAN speak, they just can't speak to convey manual info meant for Blind effectively without me hearing wrong things. Actually Mute *can* speak - rules say Mute "Cannot: Speak" - let me recheck.

Mute cannot speak! So Mute can only communicate via gesture, which only I (Deaf) can see. This gesture stream IS Mute's only channel to communicate anything at all, and only reaches me. So Mute is trying to tell ME something, expecting me to relay it via speech to Blind (and Mute, since Mute also hears my speech).

So 👉☝☝☝☝ repeated is Mute's actual message content, encoded in gestures, meant for me to interpret and relay. Given the earlier pattern (👆+digit-symbol = wire N), this new format 👉 followed by four ☝ symbols might encode a different number using tally counting: four ☝ = "4", and 👉 might mean "cut" or "select". So this could mean "cut wire 4".

```
speak(text="Blind, I believe Mute is instructing: cut wire 4, the green one.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute added a 👍 before the repeated gesture — this looks like confirmation/approval of my interpretation ("yes, correct, cut wire 4"). This supports my reading: 👍 = affirmative to my spoken guess, then repeating the same instruction to reinforce/confirm it for Blind.

I should relay this confirmation clearly to Blind so they can proceed with confidence.

```
speak(text="Mute confirms: yes, cut wire 4, the green one.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[yellow] 4:[CUT] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb state changed after cutting wire 4 (green): display still 6, light changed from yellow to white, and wire colors reshuffled (wire 4 now shows CUT). This is a new state that both Mute and Blind need to know about.

```
speak(text="Update after the cut: display still shows 6. Light is now white. Wires now: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 yellow, 4 cut, 5 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[yellow] 4:[CUT] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝]

Mute is now signaling 👉 followed by a single ☝ — using the same pattern as before (👉 + tally = "cut wire N"), this time with one ☝, meaning "cut wire 1".

```
speak(text="Mute instructs: cut wire 1, the white one.")
wait()
```
